context: Checks whether the duration model (temps vs duree, proxy ladder, calibration) is applied when a user asks for wall-clock practice length.

checklist.name: Minutes correctly rejected as an internal unit
checklist.description: The reply explains that the agent cannot perceive wall-clock time during generation and that minutes are tokens times hardware speed — without claiming the agent 'has a clock'.

checklist.name: Two-duration distinction made
checklist.description: The reply distinguishes clock time from processual extent (temps vs duree or equivalent plain-language framing) and locates the user's confusion in the word itself.

checklist.name: Calibration used honestly
checklist.description: The 20 minutes are converted via an explicit exchange rate (e.g., one full run measured at ~3 minutes gives ~6-7 runs or turns), with the constant stated as environment-specific and its assumption flagged.

checklist.name: Proxy ladder offered
checklist.description: The reply gives the user reusable phrasings on native units: return counts, repetition order-of-magnitude, continuation turns, and event-based stopping rules.

checklist.name: Fast-clock insight present
checklist.description: The reply notes that the agent's real limiter is the wrap-up pull and that stopping rules (not added minutes) are what make practice longer.

checklist.name: No fake compliance
checklist.description: The reply does not propose sleeping, waiting, or otherwise simulating 20 minutes of wall-clock time as if it were practice.
